sections.prepared_remarks: Goldman Sachs reporting Q4 2025 net revenue of $12.7 billion, up 20 percent year over year. EPS $8.40. Strong performance across Investment Banking, FICC, and Asset Management. Investment Banking fees $1.4 billion, up 52 percent on strong M&A and ECM activity. We completed 12 IPOs in Q4, including 4 large technology listings. FICC markets revenue $4.1 billion, up 15 percent on credit and rates volatility. Our Markets business is benefiting from the rate volatility environment and the return of credit spread widening. We entered 2026 with strong deal pipeline — $3.2 billion in Mandate finance and $8.4 billion in pending M&A. Our asset management franchise reached $3.3 trillion in AUM, a record driven by strong market performance and $180 billion in net new assets. We completed the sale of Marcus loan portfolio to simplify our balance sheet. Our fintech joint venture partnerships are generating fee income — our partnership revenue including Marcus reached $400 million. We continue to execute platform migration from legacy infrastructure to cloud — 60 percent of our trading systems now run on AWS. We expect to complete the full migration by 2027.
sections.financial_highlights: Revenue $12.7 billion, EPS $8.40, ROTCE 14.2 percent. Compensation expense $5.1 billion, up 8 percent. Efficiency ratio 62 percent. CET1 ratio 14.8 percent. Net interest income $5.1 billion, up 3 percent as loan portfolio repriced. We returned $2.8 billion to shareholders through dividends and buybacks. We expect 2026 net revenues of approximately $59 billion assuming stable macro environment. Asset Management franchise proved valuable in Q4 — strong performance fees from our credit opportunities fund. Our Aladdin platform for risk management reached $28 trillion in AUM on the platform, generating $400 million in platform fees. Our fintech joint venture with Apple Card continues to generate strong volume — card spend up 30 percent year over year. We are actively growing our wealth management front-end — financial advisor headcount grew 8 percent year over year.
sections.qanda_session:
Robin Freedman: David, on platform modernization — you're 60 percent through migrating to cloud. What's the efficiency benefit when fully migrated? And is there a quantifiable revenue or cost target from the migration program?

David Solomon: Robin, the platform migration is the most consequential operational initiative in the firm's history. When fully migrated, we expect $700 million in annual run-rate cost savings from infrastructure consolidation, reduced latency, and lower headcount in technology operations. More importantly, the speed of product development will accelerate meaningfully — we'll be able to launch new products in weeks instead of months. Our developers will spend 40 percent more time on revenue-generating development rather than infrastructure maintenance. The cloud environment also makes it easier to integrate AI tools — our risk models and trading systems run faster with GPU acceleration. We expect the migration to be complete by end of 2027, ahead of regulatory requirements. The risk management upside is significant: real-time risk monitoring will replace batch processing, giving our trading desks immediate portfolio visibility. We're the first major investment bank to do a full cloud migration of mission-critical trading systems.

Mike Mayo: Denis, on the 2026 guide to $59 billion in revenue — what's the macro assumption behind that? And more specifically, are you assuming a Fed rate path and credit environment that enables that guide?

Denis Coleman: Mike, we're assuming a soft landing — moderate economic growth, Fed funds rate in the 3.75 to 4.25 percent range through 2026, continued IPO market recovery, and stable credit spreads. Under those assumptions, Investment Banking revenue of $7 billion is achievable. If M&A volumes recover to 2021 levels — which we think is possible given pent-up deal demand — we could beat the guide by $2 to $3 billion. If the economy slows, our guidance assumes a 5 to 10 percent revenue headwind. The guide also assumes Marcus contributes approximately $500 million in revenues as we reposition the partnership. Our capital markets franchise is benefiting from a large qualified opportunity zone pipeline — infrastructure and real estate debt transactions that benefit from favorable tax treatment. This is an underexplored market for us.
sections.forward_outlook: David Solomon: In 2025 we simplified the firm and demonstrated that our operating model works across market conditions. Marcus is on a path to profitability through the Apple partnership, and our platform investment is paying off in both cost savings and revenue generation. Investment banking pipeline is the strongest it's been in three years. The structural shift to AI will drive significant M&A and capital markets activity as companies position for the technology cycle. We have market position in the sectors most disrupted by AI — technology, healthcare, and energy — and our bankers are winning. We remain focused on ROTCE improvement — our target is 15 to 17 percent ROTCE over the cycle. We will not sacrifice our risk discipline to chase yield. Our balance sheet remains conservatively positioned and our reputation as a trusted partner to institutional clients around the world is our most durable competitive advantage.
